seo.description: Plan your trip to Meknes: Bab Mansour & Place el-Hedim, Heri es-Souani, Royal Mausoleum, Volubilis, medina, hotels and practical tips.

name: Meknes
hero_subtitle: Bab Mansour, Place el-Hedim, Heri es-Souani and the gateway to Roman Volubilis — the Ismaili imperial city.

overview.title: Meknes: Imperial Gates, Granaries and the Road to Volubilis
overview.p1: Meknes is the majestic imperial city of Sultan Moulay Ismail: monumental gates, immense granaries, and a medina that offers a relaxed atmosphere compared to bustling Fez. Place el-Hedim and the monumental Bab Mansour set the stage, while Heri es-Souani highlights the sheer scale of ancient royal logistics.
overview.p2: Two full days allow you to explore the imperial monuments and the old medina comfortably, while a third day is perfect for visiting the nearby Roman ruins of Volubilis and the holy mountain town of Moulay Idriss Zerhoun.

places.title: Must-Visit Places in Meknes
places.subtitle: Imperial gates, ancient royal granaries, Roman ruins, and historic sites you cannot miss.

bab.title: Bab Mansour
bab.desc: One of North Africa's most magnificent and ornate imperial gateways.

hedim.title: Place el-Hedim
hedim.desc: Meknes's vibrant main square, lively with storytellers, musicians, and terrace cafés.

heri.title: Heri es-Souani
heri.desc: Vast royal stables and granaries built to withstand sieges and house imperial horses.

volubilis.title: Volubilis Archaeological Site
volubilis.desc: UNESCO-listed Roman ruins featuring exceptional preserved mosaics and triumphal arches.

ismail.title: Mausoleum of Moulay Ismail
ismail.desc: Exquisite resting place of the founder, showcasing fine Moroccan tilework and peaceful courtyards.

medina.title: Meknes Medina & Souks
medina.desc: Traditional artisan markets and peaceful residential alleys full of local charm.

medersa.title: Bou Inania Madrasa
medersa.desc: A 14th-century theological college renowned for its stunning wood carvings and zellige tiles.

jamai.title: Dar Jamai Museum
jamai.desc: A late 19th-century palace showcasing Moroccan arts, carpets, ceramics, and traditional jewelry.

idriss.title: Moulay Idriss Zerhoun
idriss.desc: A picturesque hillside pilgrimage town draped across twin green hills near Volubilis.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A balanced schedule to see the imperial highlights and Roman ruins.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Start at Place el-Hedim and admire the majestic architecture of Bab Mansour in the morning light.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Wander through the peaceful artisan souks and discover local crafts at your own pace.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Relax on a rooftop café overlooking the bustling square as evening falls.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Explore the massive royal granaries and stables, followed by a visit to the Mausoleum of Moulay Ismail.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Visit the intricate Bou Inania Madrasa and explore Moroccan artifacts at the Dar Jamai Museum.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Enjoy a slow-cooked tagine in a traditional riad courtyard.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Take a short trip out to Volubilis to walk among the ancient Roman colonnades and mosaics.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Stop by the sacred hillside town of Moulay Idriss for panoramic views and local pastries.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: A final dinner in town before your onward journey.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.desc: The medina and Place el-Hedim are easily explored on foot. Use petit taxis for quick trips to Heri es-Souani, and grand taxis or arranged transport for Volubilis.

bargain.title: Souk Bargaining
bargain.desc: Shopping in Meknes is much calmer than in Marrakech or Fez. Friendly bargaining is welcome in the souks for local handicrafts and carpets.

water.title: Stay Hydrated
water.desc: Spring and autumn offer ideal weather for walking the ruins of Volubilis and the historic ramparts. Always carry bottled water during warmer months.

daytrips.title: Best Day Trips from Meknes
daytrips.subtitle: Explore Roman history, sacred towns, and imperial neighbors within easy reach.

volubilis.title: Volubilis & Moulay Idriss
volubilis.desc: The classic combination of Roman mosaics and the sacred hillside town.

fes.title: Fez Imperial City
fes.desc: Only 30–45 minutes away by train for a full day in Morocco's spiritual capital.

atlas.title: Middle Atlas & Ifrane
atlas.desc: Alpine-style town, cedar forests, and wild monkeys in Azrou.

q1.question: How many days should I spend in Meknes?
q1.answer: 2 to 3 days is ideal to explore the imperial monuments, medina, and make a half-day trip to Volubilis.

q2.question: Is Meknes safe for tourists?
q2.answer: Yes, Meknes is very safe and much calmer than Morocco's larger tourist hubs, allowing for a relaxed travel experience.

q3.question: What currency is used and can I pay by card?
q3.answer: Morocco uses the dirham (MAD). Cards are accepted in major hotels and restaurants, but cash is needed for small shops and taxis.

q4.question: How do I get to Meknes?
q4.answer: Meknes is extremely well connected by the ONCF train network from Fez, Rabat, Casablanca, and Tangier.
